fundamental.text: Raw sugar is 2.02¢/lb above hydrous-ethanol parity in Brazil, so mills favour sugar in the mix (more supply). Sugar in BRL at R$2,302/t (58th pct of 5 yrs). The short-covering floor in raws broke on 19 Nov: once fund sell stops under the prior low were hit, consumer and trade buying could not hold it, so the large managed-money long is now the main downside risk rather than a support. Desk read: Brazil drives this: the real sliding past 6 per dollar to a 19-month low on the post-election selloff makes dollar sugar more attractive for Brazilian mills to hedge and export, which caps rallies. Monday's bounce looks like short covering rather than a change in Brazil's supply picture; Europe's weaker beet crop is a minor offset.
